Traditional Maundy Thursday Bread

Served at: Maundy Thursday

Serves 8Prep 15 minCook 30 min

Bread holds deep symbolic meaning on Maundy Thursday, commemorating the Last Supper when Jesus broke bread with his disciples. This simple, rustic bread recipe honors that tradition and is perfect for serving alongside other Holy Week meals.

Ingredients

  • 3 1/2 cups (440 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 packet (2 1/4 tsp) active dry yeast
  • 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) warm water (about 110°F/43°C)
  • 1 tsp sugar
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 2 tbsp (30 ml) olive oil

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve sugar in warm water and sprinkle yeast on top; let sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
  2. In a large bowl, combine flour and salt.
  3. Make a well in the center of the flour mixture and pour in the yeast mixture and olive oil.
  4. Stir with a wooden spoon until a dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  5. Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
  6. Punch down the dough and shape it into a round loaf; place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
  7. Cover again and let rise for 30 minutes.
  8. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
  9. Make a few shallow slashes on the top of the loaf with a sharp knife.
  10. Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.
  11. Cool on a wire rack before serving.

Tips

  • For a heartier bread, substitute half the all-purpose flour with whole wheat flour.
  • Add a tablespoon of herbs like rosemary or thyme to the dough for extra flavor.
  • Serve warm with olive oil and a sprinkle of sea salt for a traditional touch.
